check the handful of moves most likely to be counterexamples, and if none carries the label,
declare the set closed *and record that you declared it*. Thirteen in-game checks — 8 positives and
5 negatives — settled both Classifications. The full sweep stays available in
`docs/classification-survey.md` if a future native Classification ever needs exhaustive proof
instead of a judgement call.

## For consumers

1. Render **`classifications`** from `move_info` — never raw `flags`, and never a `mechanical` or
   `internal` flag dressed up as a Classification.
2. Honour `classifications_unverified`: show those as unknown, not as absent.
3. The internal key is stable and Showdown-shaped; the label is what changes. Key your storage on
   `flag`, display `official_name`.
4. Adding a new Classification is a **data** change (`data/seeds/classification.csv`) plus, for a
   Champions-native one, membership rows in `data/seeds/move_flag_champions.csv` — a hand-curated
   overlay kept separate so re-running `generate_moves.py` can never clobber it.
rules.calc_test_vectors:
# Calc Test Vectors — the conformance suite (Spec 002, Phase 1)

This is the **answer key** for the deterministic calc tools (`damage`, `speed_order`). It exists so
the authoritative Champions battle-math never has to be re-derived, re-explained, or re-reviewed: the
numbers are fixed here, checked automatically, and reusable by any other implementation.

> **Technical:** A published conformance test-vector set. The machine-readable source of truth is
> `data/calc-vectors.json` (also embedded in `dist/champions-logic.json` under `calc_vectors`).
> Each vector pairs explicit tool inputs with the expected output fields, independently hand-derived
> from `rules/damage-formula.md` and `rules/stat-mechanics.md`. CI golden-tests every vector against
> the live MCP tools on each build, so the vectors can never silently drift from the implementation;
> any mechanics change must update the vectors in the same commit or the build fails.
>
> **Practical:** A list of "here's the exact setup, here's the exact answer" examples, checked on
> every change. This server is tested against it, and so is any other app you build — an offline copy
> just has to reproduce these numbers to prove it matches the official mechanics. If we ever change
> the math, the examples and the checker move together, so they're never out of sync.

## How to use it as an oracle (offline conformance)

> **Technical:** An offline/vendored calculator (e.g. a zero-network "War Room" app) loads
> `data/calc-vectors.json` (or the `calc_vectors` block of the JSON export), runs each vector through
> its own implementation, and asserts equality on the `expect` fields. `vectors_version` increments
> when the set changes, signalling consumers to re-sync. The MCP is the source of truth; the local
> copy only has to match.
>
> **Practical:** Your offline app ships these examples and checks itself against them at startup or in
> its own tests. As long as it reproduces the answer key, it's guaranteed to agree with this server —
> no network, no re-explaining, no drift.

## Worked derivations (a few, in full)

**`dmg-stab` / `dmg-floor` — Champions truncates (always drops the decimal).**
> **Technical:** L50, 80 BP, A=120, D=100. `base = floor(floor((floor(2·50/5)+2)·80·120/100)/50)+2
> = floor(floor(22·96)/50)+2 = floor(2112/50)+2 = 42+2 = 44`. Every modifier step **truncates**
> (floor), regardless of the fraction. STAB ×1.5 (Step 7): max roll R=100 `floor(44·86…→44)` →
> `floor(66.0)=66`; min roll R=86 `floor(44·0.86)=floor(37.84)=37` → `floor(37·1.5)=floor(55.5)=55`.
> The distinguishing case is `dmg-floor` (an `other` ×1.7 on the max roll): `floor(44·1.7)=floor(74.8)
> =74` — mainline "round half down" would give **75**; Champions floors to **74**.
>
> **Practical:** The one rule to remember: after every step you just delete everything after the
> decimal point — 55.5 → 55 AND 74.8 → 74 (never rounding up). That single rule is where most
> "off by one" disagreements between calculators come from, so it's pinned here twice.

**`spd-trick-room` — Speed comparison inverts.**
> **Technical:** Garchomp neutral 0 SP = `floor((102+20+0)·1.0)=122`; Garchomp Jolly +32 SP Spe =
> `floor((102+20+32)·1.1)=floor(169.4)=169`. Without Trick Room the 169 set moves first; under Trick
> Room the **slower** set (122) moves first. Priority brackets still precede the Speed check.
>
> **Practical:** Trick Room flips "fastest first" into "slowest first" — so the 122 mon outruns the
> 169 mon while it's up. Priority moves still go first either way.

**`spd-mega-slower` — Mega can lower Speed.**
> **Technical:** Mega Garchomp's base Speed (92) is lower than Garchomp's (102), so its presented
> Speed is 112 vs 122 — the Mega is slower. The tool reads Mega stats from `mega_evolution` when
> `mega:true`.
>
> **Practical:** Mega Evolving doesn't always make you faster — Mega Garchomp is actually slower than
> regular Garchomp, and the calculator knows that from the data.

## The full set

The complete, authoritative list lives in `data/calc-vectors.json` (`vectors_version` 10; 34 vectors —
v10 only re-states the `spd-mega-slower` input with its Mega Stone: since Regulation M-C Garchomp has a
second Mega on Garchompite Z, so a bare `mega: true` is ambiguous and fails loud, as it always did for
Charizard X/Y; no expected value changed):
8 `damage` vectors (neutral, STAB, super-effective, immune, critical, spread, burn, and the
floor-not-round-half-down case), 7 `speed_order` vectors (Stat-Alignment Speed, Choice Scarf, Trick
Room, priority bracket, paralysis, Speed tie, Mega Speed), 18 `damage_matchup` vectors (neutral
mirror, Life Orb, Adaptability, immunity, 4× super-effective, resist berry, type item, Technician,
weather-applied-once, multi-hit per-hit, Fairy Aura Mega, an -ate retype, Supreme Overlord,
Disguise, Light Ball, Focus Sash, Mega-form-by-stone, and Last Respects), and 1 `resolve_turn`
vector (priority/Speed-ordered exchange where the faster attacker's OHKO stops the foe from acting).
Read that file for every input/expected pair; this document explains how the suite is used and why a
few of the trickier results come out the way they do.

> **Technical:** `damage_matchup` resolves item/ability/field effects from the
> `item_effect`/`ability_effect`/`field_condition` tables (Spec 002 Phase 2). Coverage is bounded by
> the curated Champions item/ability pool; an effect outside it is reported in `unmodeled_effects`
> (`partial:true`) rather than silently dropped, so the oracle never returns a confidently-wrong
> number.
>
> **Practical:** The damage examples now include real items and abilities (Life Orb, Adaptability,
> berries, …). If you feed it something the data doesn't cover yet, it tells you instead of guessing.
rules.damage_formula:
# Damage Formula (Generation 9)

**Regulation scope:** Generation 9 core mechanic — mostly format-independent, **with one
Pokémon Champions–specific deviation (in force in every regulation to date — M-A, M-B, M-C):
the damage roll is 86–100% (15 rolls), not the standard
85–100% (16 rolls).** See Step 2 #6 and the callout below.
**Source:** Bulbapedia, "Damage" (https://bulbapedia.bulbagarden.net/wiki/Damage); cross-checked
against Pokémon Showdown mechanics. The 86–100% / 15-roll Champions damage roll is owner-specified from
the actual Pokémon Champions engine. Retrieved 2026-06-20.

> **Technical:** The Showdown `champions` mod does **not** override `Battle.randomizer`, so on
> Pokémon Showdown the damage roll is the standard 85–100% (16-roll) spread. We intentionally
> diverge on **two** owner-verified points where the real Champions engine differs from the mod /
> mainline: (1) the damage roll is **86–100%** (15 rolls); (2) **rounding** after each modifier step
> is plain **truncation (floor)** — the engine always drops the fraction — rather than the mainline
> "round half down" (pokeRound). The modifier **order** was audited 2026-06-22 against the mod's
> `modifyDamage` and matches exactly; only the roll and the rounding diverge.
>
> **Practical:** Showdown plays Champions with the normal 85% low-roll and rounds a tie down to the
> nearest whole number; the real game uses 86% and just **chops off the decimal every time**. We
> follow the real game. The *order* of the bonuses is the same as Showdown.

> ### ⚠ Champions damage roll (format-specific)
>
> **Technical:** In Pokémon Champions (every regulation to date) the random damage factor R is a uniform integer in the
> inclusive range **[86, 100]** — **15** discrete rolls. Default Showdown / Scarlet & Violet use
> **[85, 100]** — **16** rolls. Apply this at modifier-chain Step 2 #6; everything else in the
> formula is unchanged. Minimum-roll damage = `floor(base * 86 / 100)` (after prior steps).
>
> **Practical:** In this format a move's damage "low roll" is 86% of its base instead of 85%.
> Slightly less variance and a marginally higher worst case. It's the one place Champions' math
> differs from the standard games/simulators.

> **Technical:** Deterministic per-hit damage computation with explicit operation order and
> integer rounding (**truncate / floor — always drop the fraction, regardless of value**) applied
> after each modifier stage. This is the Champions rule and is uniform with the floors already taken in
> Step 1; it is NOT the mainline "round half down".
>
> **Practical:** The exact math for how much a move hurts, step by step, including where the
> game throws away fractions. After every step you just delete whatever is after the decimal
> point. Follow it top to bottom.

## Inputs

- `Level` — attacker's level (in VGC, set to 50).
- `Power` — move base power (from `move.power`).
- `A` — attacker's effective Attack (physical move) or Special Attack (special move), after
  stat stages, items, and abilities.
- `D` — defender's effective Defense (physical) or Special Defense (special), after stages,
  items, abilities. (Note: a few moves cross these, e.g. Psyshock uses the target's Defense.)

## Step 1 — Base damage

```
base = floor( floor( ( floor(2 * Level / 5) + 2 ) * Power * A / D ) / 50 ) + 2
```

Evaluate inner to outer; each `floor` truncates toward zero (values are non-negative here).

## Step 2 — Modifier chain (apply in this order)

After Step 1, multiply by each applicable factor **in this exact order**, **truncating (floor) to
an integer after each step** — in Pokémon Champions the engine always drops the fraction, regardless
of its value (e.g. `74.8 → 74`, `55.5 → 55`). (This differs from mainline Pokémon / the Showdown
mod, which round half down; the modifier *order* is identical.):

1. **Targets** — ×0.75 if the move hits multiple targets (spread move in a Double Battle) and
   there is more than one target; otherwise ×1.
2. **Parental Bond** — second hit ×0.25 (ability-specific; usually N/A).
3. **Weather** — ×1.5 (e.g., Water move in Rain, Fire move in Sun); ×0.5 (e.g., Fire move in
   Rain, Water move in Sun); else ×1.
4. **Glaive Rush / other pre-crit flat modifiers** — as applicable (usually ×1).
5. **Critical hit** — ×1.5 if the hit is a critical hit; else ×1.
6. **random (damage roll)** — multiply by a random integer R, then `floor(base * R / 100)`.
   **In Pokémon Champions, R is drawn from [86, 100] — 15 possible rolls (the
   86–100% spread).** This differs from default Pokémon Showdown / Scarlet & Violet, which draw
   R from [85, 100] — 16 rolls (the 85–100% spread). The practical effect: the minimum damage
   roll in Champions is 86% of base, not 85%, so worst-case damage is slightly higher. See the
   "Champions damage roll" callout below.
7. **STAB (Same-Type Attack Bonus)** — ×1.5 if the move's type matches one of the attacker's
   types; ×2.0 with Adaptability; Terastallized Pokémon follow Tera-STAB rules (×2.0 when Tera
   type matches original type). Else ×1.
8. **Type effectiveness** — ×(product of the attacking type vs each of the defender's types):
   each matchup ∈ {0, 0.5, 1, 2}; combined ∈ {0, 0.25, 0.5, 1, 2, 4}. A `0` anywhere ⇒ 0 damage.
   (Query `type_effectiveness`; multiply the two rows for dual-typed defenders.)
9. **Burn** — ×0.5 if the attacker is burned and the move is physical (unless the ability Guts,
   which instead removes the drop); else ×1.
10. **other** — remaining multipliers (screens ×0.5, items like Life Orb ×1.3 handled here or
    on A depending on effect, abilities, Tera Shield in some battles, etc.).
11. **Z-Move / protect chip** — ×0.25 if the move hit a protected target via a Max/Z effect.

## Step 3 — Minimum and result

- If the move connects and the computed type effectiveness is non-zero, damage is at least `1`.
- The final integer is the HP removed by that hit. Multi-hit moves repeat Steps 1–3 per hit.

> **Practical:** Compute the base number, then apply each bonus/penalty one at a time in the
> listed order, chopping off the decimal (always rounding down) after each. Type immunity (a 0)
> anywhere makes the whole thing 0. A move that lands always does at least 1.

## Notes / edge cases (consult `interactions.md`)

- Effective `A`/`D` already include stat-stage multipliers (e.g., +1 = ×1.5) computed before
  Step 1; this document assumes they are pre-resolved. **How base stats become effective stats in
  Champions — perfect IVs (+20), SP (Stat Points, 66 pool / 32 per stat, replacing EVs), and
  Stat Alignment (the renamed Nature) — is in `stat-mechanics.md`.**
- Some moves use the opponent's stat, the physical/special split exceptions, or ignore stat
  changes (e.g., critical hits ignore the attacker's negative offensive stages and the
  defender's positive defensive stages).
- Fixed-damage moves (e.g., Seismic Toss, Night Shade) bypass this formula entirely.
rules.move_resolution_order:
# Move Resolution Order (Generation 9)

**Regulation scope:** Generation 9 core mechanic — format-independent (applies under M-C and
all SV regulations); framed for the Double Battle (VGC) format.
**Source:** Bulbapedia, "Priority" and "Speed"
(https://bulbapedia.bulbagarden.net/wiki/Priority); Smogon mechanics guides. Retrieved
2026-06-20.

> **Technical:** Deterministic turn-sequencing algorithm — pre-move actions, then move
> execution ordered by priority bracket, then effective Speed (with Trick Room inversion and
> random speed-tie resolution), then end-of-turn residuals.
>
> **Practical:** The order things happen in a turn: what goes first, how ties break, when
> switches and weather damage land.

## Phase A — Start of turn (before any moves)

Resolved in this order:

1. **Terastallization** — a Pokémon that chose to Terastallize does so now, before move
   execution.
2. **Pre-move actions** — fleeing (not in VGC), using a Bag item (not in VGC), and **manual
   switches** execute before any attack. When multiple Pokémon switch, the faster Pokémon's
   switch resolves first (Speed order).

## Phase B — Move execution order

Each Pokémon's move is ordered by, in precedence:

1. **Priority bracket** (highest first). Move priority ranges roughly −7…+5 (from
   `move.priority`). Examples: Protect/Detect +4, Fake Out +3, Extreme Speed +2, Quick
   Attack/Aqua Jet +1, normal 0, Avalanche −4, Trick Room −7.
2. **Priority-altering abilities/items** within the same nominal move:
   - **Prankster** +1 to status moves (and the move fails against Dark-types).
   - **Gale Wings** +1 to Flying moves at full HP. **Triage** +3 to healing moves.
   - **Quick Claw** (20% chance) / **Quick Draw** (30%, damaging) / **Custap Berry** (≤25% HP):
     act first **within** their priority bracket.
   - **Lagging Tail / Full Incense / Stall**: act **last** within their bracket.
3. **Effective Speed** (higher acts first) for moves sharing a bracket. Effective Speed
   includes stat stages, items (Choice Scarf ×1.5), abilities, Tailwind (×2), paralysis (×0.5
   in Gen 7+), and field effects.
4. **Trick Room** inverts Speed comparison within each bracket (lower effective Speed acts
   first) while active.
5. **Speed tie** — if two Pokémon have identical effective Speed in the same bracket, the order
   is chosen **randomly** (50/50). This is the only non-deterministic ordering point.

> **Practical:** Higher-priority moves (like Protect or Fake Out) always go before normal ones.
> Among moves with the same priority, the faster Pokémon goes first — unless Trick Room is up,
> which flips it so the slower one goes first. Exact Speed ties are a coin flip.

## Phase C — End of turn (residual order)

Residual effects resolve in a fixed order after all moves, including (high level):

1. Weather damage (Sandstorm) and weather changes ending.
2. Future Sight / Doom Desire strikes.
3. Wish healing.
4. Status damage: Burn, Poison/Toxic (Gen 8+ ordering by Speed among afflicted).
5. Item/ability residuals: Leftovers, Black Sludge, Leech Seed, Aqua Ring, Ingrain, Speed Boost.
6. Field/condition timers tick down: Trick Room, Tailwind, screens (Reflect/Light Screen),
   Safeguard, Terrain, weather.

(Within a residual step, ties between Pokémon are broken by Speed, subject to Trick Room.)

## Determinism note

All ordering is deterministic **except** the explicit speed-tie coin flip (Phase B.5) and
chance-based priority items/abilities (Quick Claw, Quick Draw). Everything else is a pure
function of priority, effective Speed, and active field effects.
rules.interactions:
# Interaction Rulings (Generation 9)

**Regulation scope:** Generation 9 core mechanics — format-independent unless a specific
regulation overrides (none known for M-C).
**Source:** Bulbapedia / Smogon mechanics; the **Status conditions** section + the Unseen Fist /
Healer entries are from the Champions mod's runtime code (`data/mods/champions/conditions.ts`,
`abilities.ts`), corroborated by Champions patch-note coverage. Retrieved 2026-06-20 (status
mechanics 2026-06-22). **The Healer and Unseen Fist values were confirmed IN-GAME by the owner on
2026-07-30** (source 17) — the mod is not automatically the game (it uses the standard 85% damage
roll where the game uses 86%), so these two now rest on observation, not inference. Entries here are the commonly re-asked interactions; expand as questions recur.

> **Technical:** A curated ruling set for non-obvious interactions not captured by the damage
> formula or the resolution order alone.
>
> **Practical:** The "but what about…" answers — the tricky combos people keep asking about.

## Type & immunity interactions

- **Dual-type effectiveness** is the product of the attacking type vs each defending type
  (`type_effectiveness`): possible totals 0, 0.25, 0.5, 1, 2, 4. Any single 0 ⇒ total 0.
- **Terastallization** changes the defender's type for effectiveness and changes the
  attacker's STAB; a Pokémon's Tera type fully replaces its original typing for type-matchup
  purposes while keeping STAB on its original type(s) per Tera-STAB rules.
- **Ground immunity sources**: Flying type, Levitate, Air Balloon, Magnet Rise, Telekinesis —
  any of these makes Ground moves miss (0×), independent of the type chart.

## Priority & speed interactions

- **Prankster** gives status moves +1 priority but they **fail against Dark-type** targets.
- **Psychic Terrain** blocks priority moves from hitting grounded targets.
- **Trick Room** inverts speed order within each priority bracket; it does **not** change
  priority brackets themselves (Protect still goes first).
- **Choice Scarf** ×1.5 Speed; **Tailwind** ×2 Speed; both feed *effective Speed*, not priority.

## Protect family

- Protect/Detect/Spiky Shield/etc. (+4 priority) block most moves for that turn; consecutive
  use has a decreasing success chance (×1/3 each consecutive turn).
- Spread/Max moves chip through some protects; Feint and Unseen Fist bypass Protect.
- **Unseen Fist (Champions):** a contact move bypassing Protect this way deals **×0.25 damage**
  through the protection (formula's `bypassProtect` step) — a Champions nerf vs the standard
  ability, which bypasses at full damage. **Owner-verified in-game 2026-07-30.** Note the standard
  "except Max Guard" wording does not apply: Max Guard is a Dynamax mechanic and Champions has no
  Dynamax.

## Item / ability damage interactions (feed the formula's modifier chain)

- **Life Orb** ×1.3 damage, 10% recoil. **Choice Band/Specs** ×1.5 to Atk/SpA (locks move).
- **Light Ball** doubles **Pikachu's** Attack and Sp. Atk (holder-gated — no effect on any other
  species). Applied at the effective-stat step, so it stacks with STAB and type-boost items.
- **Reflect / Light Screen / Aurora Veil** ×0.5 damage taken (×2/3 in Doubles) for the
  relevant category.
- **Burn** halves physical damage (formula Step 9) unless **Guts** (which boosts Atk instead).
- **Multiscale / Shadow Shield** ×0.5 damage when at full HP.
- **Focus Sash** — a holder at **full HP** survives an otherwise-lethal single hit with **1 HP**
  (single use), identical in effect to the **Sturdy** ability. `damage_matchup` reflects this in the
  `ko` label ("survives the first hit (Focus Sash, 1 HP)"); against a multi-hit move it only blocks
  the first hit (flagged, not modeled).
- **Last Respects** base power = 50 × (1 + number of fainted allies on the **user's** side), capped
  at a 6-Pokémon team (≤5 fainted → max 300 BP). In the calc, pass `fainted_allies` (the same input
  Supreme Overlord uses). **Rage Fist** scales with hits **taken** this battle, which the one-turn
  calc doesn't track — it fails loud rather than report its flat listed power.

### Selecting a Mega form in the calc tools

A Pokémon with **two** Mega forms (**Charizard**: Mega-X is Fire/Dragon, Mega-Y is Fire/Flying;
since M-C also **Absol, Garchomp and Lucario**, whose Z stones give Absol-Mega-Z, Garchomp-Mega-Z
and Lucario-Mega-Z beside the regular Megas) is disambiguated by the **held Mega Stone** (Charizardite X → Mega-X, Charizardite Y →
Mega-Y), an explicit `mega_form` field (`"X"`/`"Y"`), or by naming the Mega directly as the
`species` (`"Charizard-Mega-Y"`). The form changes the typing — e.g. Rock is **4×** on Mega-Y but
**2×** on Mega-X — so the right form must be chosen for the type chart to be correct. A `mega:true`
request with no way to tell the forms apart fails loud rather than guessing.

## Status conditions (Champions-specific changes)

Pokémon Champions re-tunes the non-volatile status conditions vs the standard Gen 9 games (these
live in the mod's runtime `conditions.ts`, not the data tables):

- **Paralysis:** **1/8 (12.5%)** chance to be fully paralyzed on a given turn — *not* the standard
  1/4 (25%). The Speed penalty is unchanged (**×0.5** effective Speed; see Priority & speed).
- **Sleep:** lasts **2–3 turns** (was 1–3): on infliction the sleeper is locked for 2 or 3 turns
  (≈1/3 chance of the shorter 2-turn sleep), waking at the start of the turn after it elapses.
- **Freeze:** thaws **within ~3 turns** — a hard cap (a 3-turn timer) *plus* the usual 1/4 (25%)
  per-turn thaw chance and the normal thaw-on-fire-move / defrosting-move rules. Standard Gen 9
  freeze has no timer and can persist indefinitely on the 20%/turn check.
- **Healer (ability):** **50%** chance to cure an ally's status each turn (Champions buff; standard
  is 30%). **Owner-verified in-game 2026-07-30** — do not "correct" this back to 30% because a
  Showdown dex says so.

> **Technical:** `par.onBeforeMove` → `randomChance(1,8)`; `slp.onStart` → `sample([2,3,3])`;
> `frz` → `startTime=3` with thaw on `time<=0 || randomChance(1,4)`. These are status *durations/
> chances* only; type-immunity to a status, Safeguard/Misty Terrain blocking, etc. are unchanged.
>
> **Practical:** In Champions, full-paralysis is half as likely, sleep is a tighter 2–3 turns, and
> freeze always thaws within about three turns instead of possibly locking you forever — so status
> is less swingy than in the standard games. Factor this into "how risky is this status?" calls.

## Field & weather

- **Weather** Sun/Rain modify Fire/Water damage (formula Step 3) and some abilities/moves.
- **Terrains** (Electric/Grassy/Psychic/Misty) boost or block specific move types for grounded
  Pokémon and interact with priority (Psychic Terrain) and status (Misty/Electric).

> **Practical:** Most of these are "this item/ability/field quietly changes the number or the
> order." When in doubt, check whether the effect changes a *stat*, a *multiplier in the damage
> steps*, or the *turn order* — that tells you where it applies.

## Champions-specific ability and item rulings (from the mod's runtime code)

Champions changes a few abilities and items in ways the base-game descriptions do not state. These
are implemented in the Showdown Champions mod's runtime code (`abilities.ts` / `items.ts` handlers,
not the data fields), so they are mirrored here by hand — the same class as Healer 50% and Unseen
Fist ¼. Mod commits of 2026-09-10 to 2026-09-13; Serebii's Champions dex corroborates the first two.

- **Run Away grants immunity to trapping.** The holder ignores every effect that would prevent it
  from switching out (Mean Look, Block, Arena Trap, Shadow Tag, …). In the main-series games Run
  Away has no competitive use; here it is a real ability (Thievul). The `ability` row states this.
- **Double Shock is a Punching move** in Champions: it carries the `punch` flag, so Iron Fist boosts
  it and it shows the **Punching** Classification (Pawmot). It is not a punching move in mainline.
- **Eject Button does not cancel the attacker's own switch.** If a self-switching move (U-turn,
  Volt Switch, Flip Turn, Parting Shot) triggers the target's Eject Button, the attacker still
  switches out as well — mainline suppresses the attacker's switch in that case. `resolve_turn`
  does not model switching; it flags any turn involving Eject Button as partial.
- **Guard Dog** also blocks forced switches (Roar, Whirlwind, Red Card, Dragon Tail) in addition to
  its Intimidate reversal — as in mainline; listed because Serebii's Champions text spells it out.

## Gaps

This file is intentionally non-exhaustive. When a new interaction question recurs, add a
sourced entry here rather than relying on model recall (constitution Principle II).
rules.regulation_rules:
# Regulation M-C — Format Rules (Pokémon Champions)

**Regulation scope:** Pokémon Champions, Regulation Set **M-C** (the current regulation; this
document is regulation-agnostic in name — `regulation-rules` — and is rewritten when the regulation
changes; the previous sets are summarized in `changelog.md`).
**Active:** 9 September 2026 – 2 December 2026 (Pokémon.com: Tue 8 Sep 2026 7:00 p.m. PDT to
Tue 1 Dec 2026 5:59 p.m. PST — in-game Ranked Battles, three seasons).
**Sources:** Serebii (https://www.serebii.net/pokemonchampions/rankedbattle/regulationm-c.shtml and
its "Available Pokémon" / items pages); Pokémon.com announcement. Retrieved 2026-09-09.

> **Technical:** The format's eligibility predicate and team-construction constraints for M-C —
> the rules that gate what a legal team may contain, distinct from the per-Pokémon legality
> lists in the database (`species` / `mega_evolution` / `item` / `move` / `ability`, all scoped
> `regulation = 'M-C'`).
>
> **Practical:** The rulebook for building a legal M-C team — what's allowed, what's capped, and
> what changed from last season.

## Eligibility (what Pokémon are legal)

- **No species are restricted this season.** Every Pokémon eligible in Regulation M-A or M-B
  remains eligible, and Pokémon.com's announcement adds "24 Pokémon newly available for battle".
- M-C is the **third Mega format**: the M-B roster (208 base Dex numbers + 27 alternate formes)
  plus **23 new Dex numbers** — Wigglytuff, Persian (Kantonian **and Alolan**), Farfetch'd,
  Mr. Mime, Swalot, Salamence, Gogoat, Golisopod, Rillaboom, Cinderace, Inteleon, Thievul,
  Toxtricity (Amped **and Low Key**), Grapploct, Perrserker, Sirfetch'd, Pincurchin, Indeedee (male
  **and female** — Indeedee-F was explicitly Illegal in M-B), Pawmot, Arboliva, Squawkabilly (all
  four plumages), Mabosstiff, Baxcalibur — and **6 new Mega Evolutions** (below). The database
  holds **264 legal species rows** (231 base Dex numbers + 33 alternate formes) and **82 Megas**.
- Galarian Farfetch'd and Galarian Mr. Mime are **not** legal: Serebii lists only the Kantonian
  icons for #083 / #122, and their Champions dex pages show no alternate form (Sirfetch'd and
  Perrserker are separate Dex numbers and are legal).

> **Technical:** **Floette forme restriction.** The only legal Floette is the Eternal Flower
> forme — Showdown id `floetteeternal`, name **Floette-Eternal** (stats 74/65/67/125/128/92, Fairy,
> abilities Flower Veil / Symbiosis). The standard Floette is **not** legal and is not in the `species`
> table. Floette-Eternal carries its signature move **Light of Ruin** (Fairy, 140 BP) and a Mega
> Evolution, **Floette-Mega** (ability Fairy Aura, triggered by the Floettite stone).
>
> **Practical:** You can only use the special "Eternal Flower" Floette in Champions, not the common
> one. It comes with its signature move Light of Ruin and can Mega Evolve.

## Gimmick: Mega Evolution (the only one enabled)

The **enabled battle gimmick for M-C is Mega Evolution only** (`regulation_gimmick` =
`(M-C, mega)`), as in M-A and M-B. The Champions engine also has verified code for
**Terastallization** and **Gigantamax** (and thus Dynamax), but **no gimmick other than Mega has
ever been enabled** in a regulation — see `gimmicks.md` and the `gimmick` / `regulation_gimmick`
tables.

Per-entry legality across every regulation to date (M-A / M-B / M-C) lives in `format_legality`
— one explicit verdict per (format, entity): `legal`, `unavailable` (not in the game for that
format), `banned` (none to date) or `restricted` (none). `is_legal` returns it, with an optional
`format`; a `null` status means **no ruling recorded**, not banned. See `format-legality.md`.

- A team **may include more than one Mega Stone**, but you **may Mega Evolve only one Pokémon
  per battle**.
- **Every Mega Evolution in the roster is allowed — there are no Mega exclusions in M-C** (nor
  were there in M-A/M-B: nothing has ever been banned in Champions — see `format-legality.md`).
  The three Z Megas are **new to the game in M-C** — **Mega Lucario Z**, **Mega Garchomp Z** and
  **Mega Absol Z** (they did not exist before; owner-observed, source 29) — alongside three new
  ordinary Megas: **Mega Salamence**, **Mega Golisopod**,
  **Mega Baxcalibur**.
- A **Z Mega** is a second Mega of a species that already had one, reached through its own stone:
  Absolite → Absol-Mega (Dark, Magic Bounce) vs **Absolite Z → Absol-Mega-Z (Dark/Ghost,
  Sharpness)**; Garchompite → Garchomp-Mega vs **Garchompite Z → Garchomp-Mega-Z (pure Dragon,
  Levitate, 108/130/85/141/85/151)**; Lucarionite → Lucario-Mega vs **Lucarionite Z →
  Lucario-Mega-Z (Fighting/Steel, Aura Guard, 70/100/70/164/70/151)**. Like Charizard X/Y, the
  **held stone decides the form**; `species_info` lists both and `mega_list(stone=…)` filters.
- Mega abilities in Champions diverge from other games — take them from `mega_list` /
  `ability_info`, never from memory. The six new Megas' abilities as recorded here: Mega Salamence
  Aerilate, **Mega Golisopod Tough Claws** (Serebii's Champions dex and its Mega-abilities page;
  Pokémon Showdown's placeholder says Emergency Exit — **owner-verified in-game 2026-09-09**), Mega
  Baxcalibur Thermal Exchange, Mega Absol Z Sharpness, Mega Garchomp Z Levitate, Mega Lucario Z
  **Aura Guard** (Champions-native: "reduces damage received from moves that make physical contact
  by 50%" — **owner-verified in-game 2026-09-09**).

## Team-construction clauses

- **Species Clause**: a team cannot contain two Pokémon with the same Pokédex number.
- **Item Clause**: no two Pokémon on a team may hold the same item.
- Each Pokémon may hold one item.
- (Unchanged from M-A and M-B.)

## Legal held items are a curated, closed list (definitive)

> **Technical:** Regulation M-C does not grant open item access. The legal held-item set is a
> specific, **closed** selection — **57 hold items + 28 Berries + 81 Mega Stones = 166** (the `item`
> table, sourced from the Serebii Champions items page). M-C **added 12 held items** — Air Balloon,
> Binding Band, Eject Button, Electric Seed, Grassy Seed, Leek, Misty Seed, Normal Gem, Psychic
> Seed, Red Card, Rocky Helmet, Terrain Extender — and **6 Mega Stones** (Absolite Z, Baxcalibrite,
> Garchompite Z, Golisopite, Lucarionite Z, Salamencite); nothing was removed. Main-series
> competitive staples that are still **absent** — Choice Band, Choice Specs, Assault Vest, Eviolite,
> the type Plates — are simply **not legal**. Their absence is the format definition, not a data gap
> or an incomplete import. The `item` table is the **authoritative legal item set**; do not add
> items to "match" other formats, and do not treat a missing staple as a bug.
>
> **Practical:** Champions hands you a fixed, hand-picked box of items — bigger than last season
> (twelve new ones, including Rocky Helmet and Air Balloon) but still a closed list. If a famous
> item (like Choice Band) isn't in the database, that's correct: it isn't allowed. The item list in
> the database is the final word.

## Move pool changes in M-C

The Champions move pool is curated too (`move` table, **515 moves**). The M-C newcomers bring
**15 moves** into it: Court Change, Double Shock, Drum Beating, Glaive Rush, Jaw Lock, Meteor
Assault (**170 BP** in Champions, re-tuned from 150), Milk Drink, Octolock, Overdrive, Pyro Ball,
Revival Blessing, Shift Gear, Slash (**80 BP**, re-tuned from 70), Snipe Shot (85 BP), Zing Zap.
Serebii's in-game move list also shows **Strength Sap and Wish at 8 PP** (they were 12 in M-B) —
**owner-verified in-game 2026-09-09**, as are the Meteor Assault (170) and Slash (80) re-tunes above.
The newcomers' movesets were reconciled against the Showdown mod's M-C data on 2026-09-09: identical
for all 29 species/formes, and the mod's one omission (Meteor Assault on Sirfetch'd — **owner-verified in-game 2026-09-09**)
was fixed upstream on 2026-09-10. The mod also records that **Milk Drink can target an ally** and that
**Double Shock is a Punching move** (Iron Fist boosts it) in Champions.

## Battle-mechanics deviation — damage roll

Pokémon Champions uses an **86–100% damage roll (15 possible rolls)**, not the default 85–100%
(16 rolls) of Pokémon Showdown / Scarlet & Violet, in every regulation to date. This is the one
place Champions' damage math differs from the standard games and simulators. Full detail and where
it applies in the formula are in `damage-formula.md` (modifier-chain Step 2 #6).

## Event rules are separate

The rules above govern what a **legal team** is. How a **tournament** is run — **all Champions
tournaments are open team sheet**, and a player's notes must start **blank** (simple geometric
shapes for layout only) — is in `tournament-rules.md`.

## Notes

- These format rules are stored as Markdown (procedural) per constitution Principle III; the
  per-species/item/move/ability legality lists are stored in SQLite (`regulation = 'M-C'`).
- What a regulation *changed* is the `changelog.md` entry for it; what a regulation *is* lives here.
- The Pokémon Showdown Champions mod — the primary source for learnsets and the move pool — **lags
  the game at a regulation boundary** (on M-C day 1 it still marked every newcomer Illegal). Where
  it lagged, the data was taken from Serebii's Champions pages and says so row by row (`source_id`
  21 / 23 / 24); see `divergence-from-showdown.md`. **The mod shipped its M-C data later the same day
  and agreed with every Serebii-sourced row**, so the newcomers, formes, items and moves cite the mod
  again; upstream fixed its one gap (Meteor Assault) on 2026-09-10, so from 2026-09-14 no M-C row
  rests on Serebii alone — Serebii and the owner's in-game checks stand as the verification record.
rules.format_legality:
# Format Legality — one explicit verdict per entry, per rulebook

> **Technical:** Spec 004. Legality is a property of the **(format, entity)** pair, not of the
> entity. The `format` table registers every ruleset Champions has been played under (one per
> regulation to date — M-A, M-B, M-C — with a `kind` axis so a second concurrent ruleset can be
> added as a row); the `format_legality` table holds **exactly one explicit verdict per (format,
> entity)** for every species, Mega Evolution, ability, item, move and gimmick. Status is never
> inferred from a missing row. The entity tables keep **legal-only coverage** for the current
> regulation (row present = legal), so nothing that reads them changes meaning.
>
> **Practical:** A list of rulebooks, and for every Pokémon, Mega, item, ability, move and gimmick
> a written-down verdict under each rulebook: allowed, not in the game, banned, or limited. Every
> verdict says where it came from. If something is not on the list at all, the answer is "we have
> no ruling for that", never "no".

## The four verdicts (`format_legality.status`)

| status | meaning | exists in the data today? |
|---|---|---|
| `legal` | usable in that format | yes |
| `unavailable` | **not in the game** for that format — introduced in a later regulation, a gimmick the format does not enable, or a forme the game does not offer | yes |
| `banned` | the game or its announcement **explicitly forbids** something the game contains | **no — never, to date** |
| `restricted` | usable with a limit (`limit_count`, e.g. at most 1 per team) | no |

**Nothing has ever been banned in Pokémon Champions.** Things only *arrive*. The Z Megas (Absol /
Garchomp / Lucario-Mega-Z) did not exist in M-A or M-B; they were introduced in M-C
(owner-observed in-game, source 29). Serebii's M-B page lists them under "Mega exclusions", and
this resource had repeated that as "banned" until 2026-09-16 — a misreading, now corrected
everywhere. The `banned` status stays wired and tested so a real future ban is one data row away.

## "No ruling recorded" is its own answer

> **Technical:** `is_legal` returns three distinct shapes: `{legal: true, status: "legal"}`;
> `{legal: false, status: <banned|restricted|unavailable>, ruling: {reason, source}}`; and
> `{legal: null, status: null, ruling_recorded: false, note}`. The third is what an unknown name
> gets. `null` is falsy in every consumer language, so a yes/no caller behaves as before, while a
> careful caller can no longer read "never checked" as "not allowed".
>
> **Practical:** If you ask about something the resource has never heard of — a typo, a mainline
> item that is not in Champions — it tells you it has no ruling, instead of saying "banned".
> Re-check the spelling; slug, Showdown id and display name all work.

## Which format is answered

The current format is the newest `format.active_from` (M-C). Pass `format` to `is_legal` for a
past season (`M-A`, `M-B`); `server_info.formats` and `getting_started.formats` list them, newest
first, with each one's enabled gimmicks.

## Entities with a verdict but no data row

The entity tables hold only what is legal now. Five formes of rostered Dex numbers that the game
does not offer are recorded as `unavailable` in every format with a `display_name` and no stats:
**Farfetch'd-Galar, Mr. Mime-Galar, Qwilfish-Hisui, Floette** (base forme — only Floette-Eternal
is rostered) and **Greninja-Bond**. **Owner-verified in-game (source 29): they do not exist in the
game.** The Showdown Champions mod agrees (Illegal; source 27 for the M-A/M-B snapshots). Cosmetic formes with identical stats (the
Pikachu caps) are not modeled as entities at all; Greninja-Ash is battle-only. The generator
re-validates the list against the mod on every run, so if one ever becomes legal the build stops.

## How the backfill was derived (precedence order)

1. `banned` — the entry is in the generator's explicit ban list. **Empty.**
2. `unavailable` — `introduced_in` is newer than the format's regulation (derived, source 28,
   reason `introduced in M-C`); a gimmick the regulation does not enable (source 11); or one of
   the five formes above.
3. `legal` — otherwise; cites the entry's `introduced_source_id` (the Serebii page or the mod
   commit that attests its arrival; later formats carry it forward).

Counts (guarded by `generate_format_legality.py` and re-derived by a test): 1 252 verdicts per
format — M-C 1 244 legal / 8 unavailable; M-B 1 161 / 91; M-A 1 077 / 175; zero banned or restricted.

## Gimmicks

`regulation_gimmick` remains the **maintained** source for which gimmick a regulation enables;
the `gimmick` rows in `format_legality` are derived from it (`legal` if enabled, else
`unavailable`) and a test asserts the two agree. `is_legal("tera", "gimmick")` → `unavailable`.

## Queries

```sql
SELECT format_id, status, reason FROM format_legality
  WHERE entity_kind = 'mega' AND entity_key = 'lucariomegaz' ORDER BY format_id;   -- one entity, every season
SELECT display_name, reason FROM format_legality
  WHERE format_id = 'M-B' AND status <> 'legal' AND entity_kind = 'species';        -- what M-B did not have
SELECT * FROM format ORDER BY active_from DESC;                                     -- the rulebooks, newest first
```

## Provenance

Every verdict cites a `source` row: 26 / 2 / 21 (Serebii M-A / M-B / M-C pages), 27 (the mod's
git history), 28 (derived from `introduced_in`), 11 (owner-verified gimmick support), 12 (the
current mod), 29 (owner-observed: the Z Megas did not exist before M-C). Nothing cites source 20
(an unverified implementation default); a test asserts that. Every verdict that rests on an
in-game fact has been seen in-game by the owner (the Z Megas' absence before M-C, the five formes
above); the rest derive from `introduced_in`, whose sources are the regulation pages and the mod's
history.
rules.tournament_rules:
# Tournament Rules (Pokémon Champions events)

**Scope:** how a Champions **tournament** is run — the event-floor rules that sit *outside* the
battle engine and outside team legality. Legality and team construction live in
`regulation-rules.md`; the sheet's *layout* lives in `team-sheet-format.md`.
**Source:** **owner-provided, observed at events** (`kind='observed'` in this repo's provenance
vocabulary — the same tier that outranks Showdown/Serebii wherever they disagree). These rules are
**not** derivable from the Showdown mod, from Serebii, or from any data table: no upstream source we
hold describes them at all.

> **Technical:** Event-administration constraints — an information-disclosure policy (open team
> sheet) and a permitted-materials policy (note media) — that constrain the *player*, not the
> simulation. They are recorded here because a consumer LLM (Large Language Model) asked "what are
> the tournament rules?" will otherwise answer from mainline VGC (Video Game Championships)
> convention, which is **closed** team sheet for most of its history and has its own, different
> notes policy.
>
> **Practical:** The rules for playing at an actual tournament, as opposed to the rules for building
> a legal team. Two topics: everyone sees everyone's team sheet, and note-taking — paper only, a
> fresh empty sheet every round, and mid-match you can only read what you wrote in that match.

## 1. All tournaments are OPEN TEAM SHEET

**Every** Pokémon Champions tournament is played **open team sheet**. There is no closed-sheet
tournament format.

> **Technical:** Full pre-battle disclosure of the opponent's declared roster. The team sheet
> submitted at registration is visible to the opponent, so a player's *declared* set information is
> public knowledge for the match. This inverts the mainline default, where the sheet is submitted to
> the judge and the opponent sees only Team Preview species (plus, in newer formats, a partial
> reveal).
>
> **Practical:** Both players get to look at each other's full written team before playing. Nothing
> on the sheet is a surprise.

**Consequences that follow directly** (stated as implications, not as separately observed rules):

- A team sheet is **public information to the opponent**, so it must be accurate — it is the
  document the match is played against.
- There is **no "hide the tech"** value in a set choice; a surprise factor that depends on the
  opponent not knowing a move, item, or ability **does not exist** at a Champions tournament.
- Advice to "keep X secret" is wrong for this game. If asked to build for surprise value, say so.

**Deliberately NOT stated here** (unobserved — do **not** fill these in from mainline convention):
exactly *when* in the match flow the sheet is exchanged, whether the sheet is shown on paper or in
the client, and whether *anything* beyond the sheet's own fields (see `team-sheet-format.md`) is
disclosed. If a consumer needs those, the honest answer is "not recorded".

## 2. Notes must start BLANK — geometric shapes only

A player's notes must be **blank, as in unwritten**, at the start. The one thing permitted on the
page in advance is **simple geometric shapes for layout purposes** — a grid, boxes, columns, ruled
lines — i.e. structure to write *into*.

| Permitted in advance | Not permitted in advance |
|---|---|
| Simple geometric shapes used as layout: grid, boxes, columns, lines, table cells | Any writing: words, names, numbers |
| An empty template to fill in during the match | Pre-filled damage calcs, speed tiers, matchup notes, checklists with content |

> **Technical:** A permitted-materials rule restricting pre-match preparation carried onto the
> floor. The distinction is **content vs. container**: a container (an empty ruled grid) is legal;
> any *token carrying information* — glyph, numeral, abbreviation, tally — is not, because it is
> prepared reference material rather than an in-match record. The boundary is "unwritten", so a
> shape whose position or count itself encodes information is against the rule even though it is
> technically a shape.
>
> **Practical:** You can bring paper you've drawn a table or some boxes on, so you have somewhere
> tidy to write. You cannot bring paper with anything actually written on it — no names, no numbers,
> no notes-to-self. Empty box: fine. Box with "Chomp outspeeds" in it: not fine.

**Consequences that follow directly:**

- Pre-written cheat sheets — speed tiers, damage-calc tables, matchup crib notes — are **not**
  legal materials at a Champions tournament, however useful they'd be.
- A tool in this ecosystem that generates a "bring this to the event" reference page is generating
  something the player **may not carry onto the floor**. It can still be a *study* aid before the
  event; it must not be presented as event-legal.
- Generating a **blank** template — an empty grid to fill in by hand during the match — is legal and
  is the correct thing to offer instead.

### 2a. Paper only — no electronic notes

**Electronic note-taking is not allowed.** No phone, tablet, laptop, or app: notes are taken on
**paper**.

> **Technical:** The permitted medium is physical only. A device is disallowed regardless of whether
> its contents would satisfy the blank-start rule — the restriction is on the medium, not just on
> the content. So an "app that takes your match notes" is not an event-legal product for the floor,
> however compliant its behaviour.
>
> **Practical:** Pen and paper. No typing notes into a phone or laptop at the event.

### 2b. Fresh blank paper before every round

Notes must be taken on **blank paper before every round** — each round starts from a clean page (or
pages), carrying nothing forward in writing.

> **Technical:** The blank-start constraint in §2 re-applies **per round**, not once per event. The
> page state at the start of round *n* must satisfy the same predicate as at round 1: unwritten,
> layout shapes only. Notes therefore do not accumulate across the event on the working page.
>
> **Practical:** Every round you start with a fresh empty sheet (a pre-drawn grid is still fine).
> You don't keep adding to one sheet all day.

### 2c. Notes are allowed at all times — but in-match, only that match's notes

**Notes are allowed at all times.** The restriction is on *which* notes are usable **during a
match**: only **new notes taken during that match** may be used while it is being played.

| When | What you may write | What you may consult |
|---|---|---|
| During a match — **Team Preview included** | Yes — notes taken as the match happens | **Only** the notes taken during that match |
| Between matches / rounds / at any other time | Yes | Your notes generally (the restriction is in-match) |

**Team Preview is part of the match**, and **new notes are required** there: what you write while
reading the opponent's sheet and their Team Preview is written *inside* the match, so it is legal to
consult for the rest of it. Notes carried in from before the match are not — Team Preview is not a
loophole that lets earlier notes in.

> **Technical:** A recency scope on note *use*: writing is unrestricted in time, but the readable
> set during a match is limited to entries generated within that match. This is what makes the
> blank-start rule enforceable in practice — it forecloses consulting an earlier round's page, or
> a between-rounds preparation pass, as mid-match reference material. Combined with §2b, the
> in-match readable set always begins empty.
>
> **Practical:** Write whenever you like. But while you're actually playing a match, the only thing
> you can look at is what you wrote during *that* match — not last round's notes, and not something
> you jotted down between rounds.

**Consequence:** a between-rounds "notes to bring into the next match" artifact has no legal use
mid-match. If asked to produce one, say so.

### 2d. The page is the player's — supply it yourself, and expect it to be inspected

- **Blank pages are NOT issued by the event.** Supplying your own note paper is the **individual
  player's responsibility**. Turning up without any is your problem, not the organizer's.
- **The event may inspect your notes, at any time.** Inspection is a **right of the judging
  staff and the tournament organizer** — not a special measure requiring suspicion or cause, and
  **not restricted to between matches**: a judge may call for the page mid-match, Team Preview
  included.
- **The page is the property of the owner.** After a match, the player may do whatever they please
  with it: keep it, photograph it, publish it, bin it. Nothing is surrendered or retained.

> **Technical:** Ownership sits with the player throughout; the event holds an **inspection right**,
> not custody. The two coexist without contradiction — staff may examine the page at any point
> (that is how §2/§2a–2c are enforced on the floor: a page carrying pre-written content, or an
> earlier round's notes, is discoverable), while post-match disposition is entirely the owner's.
> Note that the inspection right plus player-supplied media is what makes the blank-start rule a
> real constraint rather than an honour system.
>
> **Practical:** Bring your own paper — nobody hands it to you. A judge is allowed to look at your
> notes whenever they like — including in the middle of a game — and needs no reason. And once the match is over the page is yours: keep it,
> post it online, throw it away, whatever you like.

**Consequence:** post-match, a player's notes are **their own material** — so a tool that helps
someone digitize, archive, or share their notes *after* a match is unproblematic. The restrictions
in §2a–2c are about what may be **carried into and read during** a match, not about what the notes
become afterwards.

## Notes on how to use this document

- These rules constrain **advice and generated artifacts**, not the calculators. `damage`,
  `speed_order` and `resolve_turn` are unaffected.
- Nothing here is in a SQLite table: it is procedural/narrative, so per constitution Principle III
  it lives as Markdown and is served as the `tournament-rules` document/resource.
- Provenance: owner-observed. Per `docs/postmortem-2026-07-30.md` §8, where Champions diverges and
  no upstream data reflects it, **only in-game/at-event observation can establish the rule** — which
  is exactly the case for everything above.
- **The notes policy (§2–2d) has no open questions left.** Every gap this document originally
  flagged as unrecorded — electronic notes, per-round pages, the in-match scope, Team Preview,
  who supplies the paper, inspection rights, post-match ownership — has since been answered by the
  owner. The **team-sheet** side (§1) still has open items; they are named there. Do not silently
  extend §2's completeness to §1.
rules.stat_mechanics:
# Stat Mechanics (Pokémon Champions) — Authoritative

**This is the single source of truth for how stats work in Champions. Read it before computing
any stat or building any set. Do NOT import Scarlet/Violet/Showdown stat conventions — the data
in this resource is Showdown-sourced but the *stat rules below are Champions-specific.***

**Source:** Owner-specified, verified in the Pokémon Champions app; the presented-stat numbers are
the canonical Generation 3–9 stat formula evaluated at Champions' fixed inputs (derivation below).

> **Technical:** Champions fixes Level = 50, IV = 31 (perfect), and replaces EVs with a 1:1
> Stat-Point (SP) pool and "Nature" with "Stat Alignment." This collapses the standard formula to
> two constants — **+75 (HP), +20 (other)** — over base stats, plus SP and an alignment multiplier.
>
> **Practical:** Everything is Level 50 with perfect IVs, so the game's shown stats are just
> **base HP + 75** and **every other base stat + 20**, before you spend Stat Points or pick a
> Stat Alignment.

## TL;DR — the locked numbers

- **Level is always 50.** Perfect IVs always (no IV customization, ever).
- **Presented (in-game) stats — default build (0 SP, neutral Stat Alignment):**
  - **HP = Base HP + 75**
  - **Atk / Def / SpA / SpD / Spe = Base + 20**
- **SP (Stat Points):** **1 SP = +1 point**, directly. Pool = **66 total**, **≤ 32 per stat**.
- **Stat Alignment** (renamed Nature): **×1.1** raised / **×0.9** lowered / **×1.0** neutral —
  applied **last**. **HP is never affected.**
- **Full presented formula (any build):**
  - `HP_presented    = Base_HP + 75 + SP_HP`
  - `Other_presented = floor( (Base + 20 + SP) × Alignment )`

That's the whole system. Everything below is justification and worked examples.

## Three distinct "stats" — never conflate them

1. **Base stats** — the species constant (e.g. Garchomp 108/130/95/80/85/102). Stored in the
   `species` (and `mega_evolution`) tables. This is the raw input; it is NOT level/IV/SP/alignment
   dependent.
2. **Presented stats** — what the game shows. Base stat run through Level 50 + perfect IV + SP +
   Stat Alignment. **This is what the MCP returns by default** (see below).
3. **Effective in-battle stat** — presented stat further modified by stat stages, items, and
   abilities. This is the `A`/`D` the damage formula (`damage-formula.md`) consumes.

## Why presented = Base + 75 (HP) and Base + 20 (other) — the derivation

Canonical Gen 3–9 formulas:
```
HP    = floor( (2·Base + IV + floor(SP_as_EV/4)) · Level/100 ) + Level + 10
Other = floor( ( floor( (2·Base + IV + floor(SP_as_EV/4)) · Level/100 ) + 5 ) · Nature )
```
At Champions' fixed inputs — **Level 50, IV 31, 0 investment, neutral:**
```
HP    = floor((2·Base + 31) · 0.5) + 50 + 10 = (Base + 15) + 60 = Base + 75
Other = floor((2·Base + 31) · 0.5) + 5       = (Base + 15) + 5  = Base + 20
```
- The **+15** is the perfect IV's contribution at Level 50 (`floor(31 · 50/100)`).
- The **+5** (other) and **+60** (HP, = Level + 10) are the formula's fixed constants.
- So **base → presented = +20 (other), +75 (HP).**

## SP — Stat Points (replaces EVs)

- **1 SP adds exactly +1** to the presented stat — a direct 1:1 conversion (NOT the EV
  `floor(EV/4)` rule; this is simpler and flatter).
- **Pool: 66 total**, distributable across the six stats; **max 32 to any single stat.**
- SP is added to the `Base + 20` (or `Base + 75` for HP) value **before** the alignment multiplier.
- (For contrast, the old EV system was 510 total / 252 per stat — Champions' SP is a small,
  even pool.)

## Stat Alignment (replaces Nature)

- **21 alignments — NOT the mainline 25.** Champions ships exactly one neutral option,
  **Serious**, and does **not** have Bashful, Docile, Hardy or Quirky. Queryable as
  `stat_alignment` (`alignment`, `raises`, `lowers`; NULL/NULL for Serious alone).
- **The whole chart below is owner-verified in-game (2026-07-30)** — all 21 names AND all 20
  raise/lower pairs, not just the roster. It previously rested on one sentence in this file saying
  the chart was *"universal and unchanged from the classic Nature chart"*: a claim about the
  raise/lower MAPPING that got silently read as covering MEMBERSHIP too, which is how four
  alignments that do not exist in this game ended up in the database for six weeks. That sentence
  is gone. If any other source disagrees with this chart, that source has not checked Champions.
- Raises one stat **×1.1**, lowers one **×0.9**, or is **neutral ×1.0**.
- **Applied LAST**, to the whole `(Base + 20 + SP)` sum, then floored. **HP is never affected.**
- Terminology only: a "Jolly Nature" is a Pokémon with **Stat Alignment: Jolly**.

| Stat Alignment | Raises ×1.1 | Lowers ×0.9 |
|---|---|---|
| Serious | — (neutral) | — (the ONLY neutral; mainline's Hardy/Docile/Bashful/Quirky are absent) |
| Lonely | Atk | Def | Brave: Atk/Spe · Adamant: Atk/SpA · Naughty: Atk/SpD |
| Bold | Def | Atk | Relaxed: Def/Spe · Impish: Def/SpA · Lax: Def/SpD |
| Timid | Spe | Atk | Hasty: Spe/Def · Jolly: Spe/SpA · Naive: Spe/SpD |
| Modest | SpA | Atk | Mild: SpA/Def · Quiet: SpA/Spe · Rash: SpA/SpD |
| Calm | SpD | Atk | Gentle: SpD/Def · Sassy: SpD/Spe · Careful: SpD/SpA |

(See the `stat_alignment` table for the exact one-raise/one-lower per alignment.)

> **Look it up, don't recall it.** Call the **`stat_alignment`** tool — by `name`, or by
> `raises`/`lowers` to get every alignment with that effect, or with no arguments for all **21**.
> It returns ready-to-apply per-stat `multipliers` and an explicit null pair for Serious.
> This chart is the single most misremembered thing in the format, in BOTH directions:
> a measured trial answered "which alignments raise Speed" with **five**, including **Quiet —
> which lowers Speed** (there are exactly four: Hasty, Jolly, Naive, Timid); and this project's
> own data claimed **25** alignments with five neutrals until an ungrounded model asserted the
> correct 21 and was scored as hallucinating. If a source tells you this chart matches another
> Pokémon game's, that source has not checked.

## Worked examples (lock these in)

**Default build — Garchomp** (Base 108/130/95/80/85/102), 0 SP, neutral:
`HP 183 · Atk 150 · Def 115 · SpA 100 · SpD 105 · Spe 122` (just +75 / +20).

**Custom set — Garchomp, Stat Alignment Jolly (+Spe / −SpA), SP 6 HP / 28 Atk / 32 Spe:**
```
HP  = 108 + 75 + 6                 = 189
Atk = floor((130 + 20 + 28) × 1.0) = 178   (Jolly neutral on Atk)
Def = floor((95  + 20 + 0)  × 1.0) = 115
SpA = floor((80  + 20 + 0)  × 0.9) = 90    (Jolly lowers SpA)
SpD = floor((85  + 20 + 0)  × 1.0) = 105
Spe = floor((102 + 20 + 32) × 1.1) = 169   (Jolly raises Spe;  ⌊169.4⌋)
```
SP check: 6 + 28 + 32 = 66 (≤ 66 ✓), each ≤ 32 ✓.

## How the MCP serves stats

- `species_info` and the JSON export return **`presented_stats`** (the default in-game numbers:
  0 SP, neutral) **and** keep the raw **`base_stats`** under their own key. Mega forms
  (`mega_evolution`) get the same `+75 / +20` transform.
- To get a *specific set's* stats, take `base_stats` and apply the **full presented formula**
  above with that set's SP and Stat Alignment. The resource provides base stats + these rules; it
  does not store per-set numbers (those depend on the build).

## Showdown/SV habits to drop (the recurring mistakes)

- **No IVs.** Never emit an `IVs:` line; to minimize a stat, use 0 SP + a lowering Stat Alignment.
- **EVs are not 510/252** — they are **SP: 66 total / 32 per stat, 1:1**.
- **"Nature" is "Stat Alignment."**
- **Do not present raw base stats as the in-game stat** — apply `+75 / +20` (and SP + alignment
  for a set). A consumer that shows Showdown base stats is showing the wrong number for Champions.
rules.team_sheet_format:
# Team Sheet Format (Poképaste / Showdown export, Pokémon Champions)

**Purpose:** the canonical layout for producing a **team sheet** (a "Poképaste"). When a team
sheet, team list, or paste-able team file is requested, format the output exactly per these
rules.
**Scope:** formatting/composition only — this does **not** govern team-building strategy.
**Source:** owner-provided template (`example_teamsheet.md`), Champions conventions.

> **Technical:** A serialized Pokémon Showdown `Set` export: per-Pokémon stanzas of ordered
> header + attribute lines + a `-`-prefixed move list, set-delimited by blank lines, with
> Champions-specific field semantics (SP in the EVs field, Stat Alignment in the Nature line,
> perfect IVs assumed).
>
> **Practical:** The standard copy-paste team format — each Pokémon as a fixed little block —
> with the Champions twist that the "EVs" are really Stat Points and "Nature" is Stat Alignment.

## Block structure (one per Pokémon)

Output each Pokémon as a stanza in **exactly this line order**:

```
<Species> (<Gender>) @ <Item>
Ability: <Ability>
Level: 50
EVs: <n> <Stat> / <n> <Stat> / ...
<Stat Alignment> Nature
- <Move 1>
- <Move 2>
- <Move 3>
- <Move 4>
```

- Separate Pokémon with **one blank line**.
- Header line: `Species (Gender) @ Item`. Use `(M)`/`(F)` for gender; omit the `(Gender)` if
  genderless. If a nickname is used: `Nickname (Species) (Gender) @ Item`. Omit `@ Item` only if
  truly itemless.
- Moves: up to four, each on its own line prefixed with `- ` (dash + space).
- Stat order in the EVs line is `HP / Atk / Def / SpA / SpD / Spe`; **omit any stat that is 0**.

## Champions-specific field semantics

- **`EVs:` line = SP (Stat Points).** Champions uses SP, but the sheet keeps the standard
  `EVs:` label for tool compatibility. The values MUST obey SP rules: **the listed numbers sum
  to ≤ 66**, and **no single stat exceeds 32**. (See `stat-mechanics.md`.)
- **`<X> Nature` line = Stat Alignment.** Champions renamed Nature to Stat Alignment, but the
  sheet keeps the `Nature` label. Use the alignment name (e.g., `Jolly Nature` = Stat Alignment
  Jolly). See the `stat_alignment` table for what each raises/lowers.
- **No `IVs:` line** — all Pokémon have perfect IVs in Champions, so IVs are never specified.
- `Level: 50` (VGC standard) unless a different level is explicitly requested.

### Gimmick lines (depend on the regulation's enabled gimmicks)

Emit gimmick-specific lines **only for the gimmicks the active regulation enables** — query
`regulation_gimmick` (and see `gimmicks.md`). Do not add lines for gimmicks that aren't enabled.

- **Mega** (enabled in M-C, as in every regulation to date): there is **no extra line** — Mega is carried by the held Mega Stone
  (the `@ <Mega Stone>` in the header). So under M-C, **do not** include a `Tera Type:` line or
  any other gimmick line.
- **Tera** (not enabled in M-C; for future Tera regulations): add a **`Tera Type: <Type>`** line
  after the Nature line.
- **Dynamax / Gigantamax** (not enabled in M-C; future): add the relevant indicator (e.g.
  `Gigantamax: Yes`) per the format in use at that time.

## Validation (enforce before emitting)

- Reject/auto-correct any set whose SP sum > 66 or whose single-stat value > 32; note the fix.
- Each Pokémon, its item, ability, and moves SHOULD be legal in the current regulation (M-C) — verify against the
  database (`species`, `item`, `ability`, `species_ability`, `move`, and `learnset`) when the
  data is available. Moves a species cannot learn (`learnset`) should be flagged.
- A team has at most 6 Pokémon; no two share a Pokédex number (Species Clause); no two hold the
  same item (Item Clause). See `regulation-rules.md`.

## The sheet is public — every tournament is open team sheet

All Champions tournaments are **open team sheet**: the opponent sees this document in full. Treat
everything on it as public information — accuracy matters more than concealment, and there is no
set choice whose value depends on the opponent not knowing it. See `tournament-rules.md`.

## Output medium

- **Markdown (default, for `.md` output):** append **two trailing spaces** to every line so the
  block renders as separate lines (Markdown hard breaks); keep one blank line between Pokémon.
- **Plain text (for a Showdown/Poképaste file or `.txt`):** no trailing spaces — emit the raw
  text exactly as above. Use this when the request is to paste into Showdown or save a paste.

## Worked example (Markdown style; trailing hard-breaks not shown)

```
Garchomp (M) @ Life Orb
Ability: Rough Skin
Level: 50
EVs: 6 HP / 28 Atk / 32 Spe
Jolly Nature
- Stomping Tantrum
- Dragon Claw
- Rock Slide
- Protect
```

(SP check: 6 + 28 + 32 = 66 ✓, max 32 ✓.)
rules.gimmicks:
# Battle Gimmicks (Pokémon Champions)

**Scope:** how the resource models battle "gimmicks" across regulations.
**Source:** owner-verified Champions engine capability (see `source` id 11) + the regulation
sources.

> **Technical:** A "gimmick" is a generation-defining battle mechanic (Mega Evolution,
> Terastallization, Dynamax, Gigantamax, …) that the Champions engine can toggle per regulation.
> The resource keeps the **active gimmick as data** — a `gimmick` catalog plus a
> `regulation_gimmick` join table — rather than hardcoding "the gimmick is Mega," so a future
> regulation can change or add gimmicks without schema changes.
>
> **Practical:** "Gimmicks" are the big special mechanics (Mega Evolving, Terastallizing, etc.).
> Instead of assuming Champions always uses Mega, the database records which gimmick(s) each
> regulation turns on — leaving room for that to change.

## Current state (important)

- **Mega Evolution is the only gimmick ever enabled** in a Champions regulation. M-A, M-B and M-C
  are all "Mega formats."
- The Champions **engine has verified code for Terastallization and Gigantamax** (and therefore
  Dynamax, its parent), but **none of these has ever been enabled** in a regulation. They are
  cataloged as `game_supported = 1`, `ever_used = 0`.

## Data model

- **`gimmick`** — the catalog: `gimmick` (id), `name`, `description`, `game_supported` (engine
  has code), `ever_used` (enabled in ≥1 regulation), `source_id`.
- **`regulation_gimmick`** — which gimmicks a regulation **enables**. Currently just
  `(M-C, mega)`. To enable Tera in a future regulation, add a row `(<reg>, tera)` — no schema
  change. This is the **maintained** source; `format_legality` carries a derived verdict per
  gimmick per format (`legal` if enabled, else `unavailable`), so `is_legal("tera","gimmick")`
  answers `unavailable` — see `format-legality.md`.
- **Per-gimmick data** lives in its own table, added only when a gimmick is enabled:
  - `mega` → `mega_evolution` (Mega formes: stats / typing / ability, keyed to base species and
    Mega Stone). Already populated.
  - `tera` → (future) legal Tera Types; per-species restrictions if Champions adds any.
  - `dynamax` / `gigantamax` → (future) Max-Move-by-type mapping and G-Max formes/moves.

## How rules and team sheets use this

- `regulation-rules.md` describes the current regulation's enabled gimmick (Mega) and its one-per-battle limit.
- `team-sheet-format.md` is **gimmick-aware**: it emits gimmick-specific lines (e.g. a
  `Tera Type:` line) only for the gimmicks the active regulation enables. Under M-C (Mega only)
  there is no `Tera Type:` line; if a future regulation enables Tera, the format adds one.

## Extending

To support a new gimmick: add a `gimmick` row (with its `game_supported`/`ever_used` and source),
enable it for a regulation via `regulation_gimmick`, add its per-gimmick data table when needed,
and add its team-sheet line to `team-sheet-format.md`. The catalog can also grow to include
Z-Moves if/when verified for Champions.
rules.changelog:
# Regulation Patch Changelog

**Purpose:** Track what changed between regulation versions/patches, each entry traceable to a
source (constitution Principle VI / FR-009).
**Status:** Regulation identity CONFIRMED — Pokémon Champions Regulation Set **M-C** (current,
9 September – 2 December 2026). The database is scoped to the current regulation only; earlier
regulations survive as the entries below.

> **Technical:** A versioned diff log of regulation rule changes (banlist deltas, restrictions,
> clause changes), each with provenance, enabling set-difference comparison across regulations.
>
> **Practical:** The "what changed in each patch" list, with a link to where each change came
> from.

## Entry format

```
### <Regulation id> — <active dates>
Source: <name + URL>, retrieved <ISO date>

- <change 1: what was banned/unbanned/restricted/clause-changed vs the prior regulation>
- <change 2 ...>
```

## Entries

### M-C — 9 September 2026 to 2 December 2026
_Data note, 2026-09-16 (server 5.2.0) — **per-entry format legality.** Every species / Mega /
ability / item / move / gimmick now carries one explicit verdict per format (`format_legality`:
legal / banned / restricted / unavailable) for M-A, M-B and M-C, so "banned", "not in the game"
and "never checked" are three different answers. **Correction, owner-observed in-game (source
29): Mega Lucario Z and Mega Garchomp Z were NEVER banned in M-B — they did not exist until M-C.**
Serebii's "Mega exclusions" wording had been repeated here as "banned"; the M-B entry below is
corrected. To date no entity has ever been banned in Champions. Five formes of rostered species
are `unavailable` in every format (Farfetch'd-Galar, Mr. Mime-Galar, Qwilfish-Hisui, base-forme
Floette, Greninja-Bond) — **owner-verified the same day: they do not exist in the game** (source
29). See `format-legality.md`._

_Data note, 2026-09-16 (server 5.1.0): every species / Mega / item / move / ability row now carries
`introduced_in` — the regulation that first made it available (M-A / M-B / M-C) — with its own
source. The M-A and M-B rosters below are therefore queryable (`WHERE introduced_in = 'M-B'`), not
just described. M-A's item pool (117) and move pool (494) were fixed from the Showdown Champions
mod's git history (source 27), since Serebii's regulation pages list Pokémon and items but never
moves; the M-B additions are exactly the six newcomers' signature moves (Barb Barrage, Make It
Rain, No Retreat, Rage Fist, Spirit Break, Topsy-Turvy). See `docs/schema-reference.md`._

Source: Serebii (https://www.serebii.net/pokemonchampions/rankedbattle/regulationm-c.shtml, plus
the "Available Pokémon", items and per-species Champions dex pages); Pokémon.com announcement
(https://www.pokemon.com/us/news/get-ready-for-regulation-set-m-c-in-pokemon-champions). Retrieved
2026-09-09. (`source_id` 21–24.)

- **Third Mega format.** Every M-A/M-B species remains eligible; **no species restricted**. Adds
  **24 newly available Pokémon** — 23 Dex numbers (Wigglytuff, Persian, Farfetch'd, Mr. Mime,
  Swalot, Salamence, Gogoat, Golisopod, Rillaboom, Cinderace, Inteleon, Thievul, Toxtricity,
  Grapploct, Perrserker, Sirfetch'd, Pincurchin, Indeedee, Pawmot, Arboliva, Squawkabilly,
  Mabosstiff, Baxcalibur) plus Alolan Persian, with Toxtricity-Low-Key, Indeedee-F (Illegal in
  M-B) and the four Squawkabilly plumages as formes — and **6 new Mega Evolutions**: Mega
  Salamence, Mega Golisopod, Mega Baxcalibur, and the Z Megas **Mega Absol Z, Mega Garchomp Z,
  Mega Lucario Z**.
- **The Z Megas are new to the game** — Mega Lucario Z, Mega Garchomp Z and Mega Absol Z did not
  exist in M-A/M-B (owner-observed, source 29; they were never banned — Serebii's "Mega exclusions"
  was a misreading). M-C has no Mega exclusions. A Z Mega is a second Mega of its species on its
  own stone (Garchompite Z), selected like Charizard X/Y.
- **12 held items added** (Air Balloon, Binding Band, Eject Button, Electric/Grassy/Misty/Psychic
  Seed, Leek, Normal Gem, Red Card, Rocky Helmet, Terrain Extender) and **6 Mega Stones**
  (Absolite Z, Baxcalibrite, Garchompite Z, Golisopite, Lucarionite Z, Salamencite): 148 → 166
  items. Nothing removed; the pool stays curated and closed.
- **Move pool 500 → 515**: Court Change, Double Shock, Drum Beating, Glaive Rush, Jaw Lock, Meteor
  Assault (170 BP), Milk Drink, Octolock, Overdrive, Pyro Ball, Revival Blessing, Shift Gear,
  Slash (80 BP), Snipe Shot, Zing Zap. Existing species that learn Slash (e.g. Charizard, Garchomp,
  Scizor — 28 of them per Serebii) gain it.
- Team-construction clauses unchanged: one Mega Evolution per battle, Species Clause, Item Clause.
- **Recorded from Serebii — and OWNER-VERIFIED IN-GAME on 2026-09-09** (source 25, a verification
  oracle; the rows keep citing the Serebii source that supplied the value): (a) **Strength Sap and
  Wish now 8 PP** (were 12; the mod, not yet updated, still implies 12); (b) **Mega Golisopod's
  ability is Tough Claws** (Showdown's placeholder entry says Emergency Exit); (c) **Aura Guard**
  (Lucario-Mega-Z) = "damage from contact moves −50%"; (d) the **Meteor Assault 170 / Slash 80**
  re-tunes. The postmortem's "the mod is not the game"
  rule cuts both ways — Serebii is a reading of the game too — which is why these were checked
  rather than trusted.
- **The three mod-vs-Serebii disagreements, settled by the owner in-game (2026-09-09, source 25):**
  Double Shock's accuracy is **100** (the mod/mainline value is kept; Serebii's "never misses" is
  wrong — `verify_serebii_sync.py` carries it as a dated known difference); **Politoed does NOT
  have Pound** and **Archaludon has neither Metal Burst nor Mirror Coat** — the Showdown mod lists
  all three, so the mod's learnsets are WRONG there and `generate_learnsets.py` now removes them
  (`OWNER_CORRECTIONS`, the first learnset rows corrected against the game). Pound thereby has no
  legal learner and joins the known orphan moves.
- **Recorded from Serebii, not owner-checked:** the 24 newcomers' learnsets (`source_id` 24). The
  owner's decision (2026-09-09) is to reconcile them against the Showdown mod when it ships its
  M-C data rather than check them in-game; until then they stand as Serebii lists them.
- **Data-provenance note.** The Pokémon Showdown Champions mod had not been updated for M-C on day
  1 (every newcomer `isNonstandard: "Past"`, no learnsets, the new items marked unavailable), so
  the newcomers' legality, learnsets and the move-pool additions come from Serebii's Champions
  pages until the mod catches up; the generators print what the mod has since caught up on.
  Separately, upstream moved the Champions-specific descriptions (Healer 50%, Unseen Fist ¼, Dire
  Claw 30%, …) out of the mod into `data/text/*.ts` (`champions:` blocks) on 2026-09-01; they are
  now ingested from there. Nothing in the runtime code (`scripts.ts`, `conditions.ts`,
  `rulesets.ts`) changed.
- **The Showdown mod shipped its M-C data later on 2026-09-09** (commit "Add Champions Regulation M-C")
  and was ingested the same day. It **agreed with every Serebii-sourced row**: the roster, the six formes
  (Galarian Farfetch'd / Mr. Mime still Illegal), the 12 items + 6 stones, Slash 80 / Snipe Shot 85,
  Strength Sap / Wish 8 PP, the same 29 Slash learners, no Pound on Politoed, no Metal Burst / Mirror
  Coat on Archaludon — and its newcomer learnsets matched the Serebii-derived rows **exactly** (0
  differences over 29 species/formes), which settles the movesets the owner chose not to check in-game.
  Two things it did not settle: it **re-tunes Meteor Assault to 170 but forgets to re-legalize it**, so
  the move and Sirfetch'd's row are kept from Serebii (**owner-verified in-game the same evening:
  Sirfetch'd knows Meteor Assault** — source 25); and it records one Champions change Serebii had only described in prose — **Milk Drink can
  target an ally** (`adjacentAllyOrSelf`), now in the data. The dated allowances were retired; the
  newcomers, formes, items and 14 moves cite the mod again. Data-only, no server change.
- **Upstream follow-up, ingested 2026-09-14** (mod commits 2026-09-10 to 2026-09-13). The mod
  **re-legalized Meteor Assault and added it to Sirfetch'd** — the one gap the M-C ingest had bridged
  from Serebii (and the owner had verified in-game) — so the last day-1 allowance is retired and every
  M-C row now comes through the mod. Three Champions rules the mod implements in code, now mirrored
  in `interactions.md`: **Double Shock is a Punching move** (Iron Fist boosts it; the `punch` flag and
  Punching Classification are in the data), **Run Away grants immunity to trapping** (the ability's
  text now says so — the base-game text "No competitive use" was wrong here), and **Eject Button
  does not cancel the attacker's own U-turn-style switch**. A companion upstream change created a
  separate `championsregmb` mod that gives Strength Sap and Wish 10 base PP *for M-B*, corroborating
  that the 8-PP values (base 5) are an M-C change. Showdown's pokedex also corrected Mega Golisopod
  to Tough Claws, agreeing with Serebii and the owner. Data-only, no server change.

### M-B — 17 June 2026 to 2 September 2026
Source: Serebii (https://www.serebii.net/pokemonchampions/rankedbattle/regulationm-b.shtml);
Pokémon.com announcement. Retrieved 2026-06-20.

- **Second Mega format.** Carries forward the entire Regulation M-A roster (186 Pokémon, 59
  Mega-capable) and **adds 22 new Pokémon and 16 new Mega Evolutions** (e.g., Mega Sceptile,
  Mega Blaziken, Mega Swampert, Mega Mawile, Mega Staraptor).
- **No species restricted** this season: all Pokémon HOME-transferable into Champions are legal.
- **No Mega exclusions.** Serebii's page lists Mega Lucario Z and Mega Garchomp Z under "Mega
  exclusions", and this entry said "banned" until 2026-09-16 — **wrong**: the owner observed in-game
  that the Z Megas did not exist until M-C (source 29). In M-B they are `unavailable`, not banned.
- Team-construction clauses unchanged from M-A: one Mega Evolution per battle, Species Clause
  (no duplicate Pokédex number), Item Clause (no duplicate items).

### M-A — (prior format)
Source: Serebii (https://www.serebii.net/pokemonchampions/rankedbattle/regulationm-a.shtml).
Retrieved 2026-06-20.

- First Mega format (the launch format, **8 April – 17 June 2026**): 186 Pokémon (185 Dex numbers +
  Floette-Eternal; 15 regional/breed formes drawn separately on Serebii's page), 59 Mega
  Evolutions (Charizard X/Y counted separately), 117 held items (incl. the launch Mega Stones),
  494 moves. Recorded 2026-09-16 as `introduced_in = 'M-A'` on every row it covers (sources 26/27).

calc_vectors.note: Conformance test vectors for the deterministic calc tools (Spec 002, Phase 1). Each entry has explicit inputs and the expected output fields. CI golden-tests every vector against the live MCP tools; an offline/vendored implementation MUST reproduce these exact values to prove it has not drifted from the authoritative Champions mechanics. Expected values are independently hand-derived from rules/damage-formula.md and rules/stat-mechanics.md, not copied from the tool. If the mechanics ever change, the vectors change in the same commit (the golden test enforces it).

vectors.description: Same, STAB x1.5 (Step 7, round-half-down). R100: 44->66; R86: 37->pokeRound(55.5)=55 (a .5 rounds DOWN).
Type effectiveness 0 -> all rolls 0, immune (no minimum-1 floor).
Critical x1.5 BEFORE the roll (Step 5): 44->66, then roll. R86: floor(66*0.86)=56; R100: 66.
Spread x0.75 (Step 1): 44->33, then roll. R86: floor(33*0.86)=28; R100: 33.
Burn x0.5 (Step 9, physical): roll then halve. R86: floor(37*0.5)=floor(18.5)=18; R100: 44->22.
M-B truncates EVERY step (never rounds a fraction up). `other` x1.7 on the max roll: floor(44*1.7)=floor(74.8)=74. Mainline round-half-down would give 75 — this vector pins the M-B floor rule.
Garchomp Jolly 32 SP Spe = floor((102+20+32)*1.1)=169 vs neutral 0 SP = 122.
Neutral Garchomp + Choice Scarf = floor(122*1.5)=183 outpaces Jolly max 169.
Under Trick Room the SLOWER set moves first: neutral 122 beats Jolly 169.
Priority bracket wins regardless of Speed: a +1 priority moves first though slower.
Paralysis halves Speed: floor(122*0.5)=61, so b (122) moves first.
Equal final Speed is a reported tie (engine-random), not a guess.
Mega Garchomp (base Spe 92 -> 112) is SLOWER than base Garchomp (122).
vectors.note: v10: names the stone — since Regulation M-C Garchomp has two Megas (Garchompite → Garchomp-Mega, Garchompite Z → Garchomp-Mega-Z), so a bare mega:true is ambiguous and fails loud, like Charizard.

vectors.description: Garchomp Earthquake vs Garchomp: eff Atk 150 (130+20), eff Def 115 (95+20), power 100 -> base 59; STAB 1.5; neutral.
Same + Life Orb final x1.3 (Step 10): 88->114, 75->pokeRound(97.5)=97.
Same but Adaptability makes STAB x2 (Step 7): min 100, max 118.
Earthquake vs Charizard (Fire/Flying): Ground x0 vs Flying -> immune.
Earthquake vs Aggron (Steel/Rock): Ground x4. Guaranteed OHKO.
Same but Aggron holds Shuca Berry (Ground resist) -> super-effective hit halved (final x0.5): max 104.
Soft Sand boosts Ground move power x1.2: 100 -> 120.
Technician boosts a <=60 BP move x1.5: Aerial Ace 60 -> 90 effective power.
Rain boosts a Water move x1.5 at the damage step ONLY (power unchanged) — regression guard against double-counting weather. Blastoise Aqua Tail vs Garchomp in rain.
Multi-hit move reports PER-HIT damage at top level; full-move totals are in the `multihit` block. Garchomp Scale Shot (Dragon, hits 2-5) vs Garchomp: per-hit 38-48 (Dragon x2 SE, STAB).
Mega Floette-Eternal's Fairy Aura boosts Fairy moves x1.33: Light of Ruin power 140 -> 186. (Mega-form ability, now modeled.)
Aerilate (Mega Pinsir) retypes a Normal move to Flying with x1.2 power: Body Slam 85 -> Flying, power 102.
One-turn exchange: Alakazam (120 Spe) Psychic vs Gengar (Ghost/Poison, x2) — Alakazam moves first by Speed and guarantees the OHKO, so Gengar never acts. Locks ordering + no unmodeled effects.
Supreme Overlord: Kingambit Iron Head with 3 fainted allies gets +10%/ally = x1.3 power (80 -> 104). Stateful ability driven by the fainted_allies input.
Disguise: Mimikyu's intact Disguise blocks the first hit entirely — Earthquake deals 0 (Mimikyu busts for 1/8 off-calc).

Light Ball doubles Pikachu's Sp. Atk (presented 70 -> 140; holder-gated to Pikachu). Thunderbolt (90 BP, STAB x1.5) vs Clefable. base=floor(floor(12*90*140/110)/50)+2=52; R86=floor(52*0.86)=44 -> STAB pokeRound(66.0)=66; R100=52 -> STAB pokeRound(78.0)=78.
Focus Sash: a full-HP holder survives a would-be OHKO with 1 HP (single use), modeled like Sturdy. Garchomp Earthquake guaranteed-OHKOs Pikachu, so the ko label becomes a survival.

ko.label: survives the first hit (Focus Sash, 1 HP)

vectors.description: Mega form selection: the held Mega Stone (Charizardite Y) resolves Charizard to Mega-Y (Fire/Flying), NOT the first-listed Mega-X (Fire/Dragon). Stone Edge (Rock) is therefore 4x (2x Fire x 2x Flying), not 2x.
Last Respects base power = listed 50 x (1 + fainted allies on the user's side). With fainted_allies=3 -> 50 x 4 = 200 effective power.
